description: A two-channel stereo mixer with a crossfader between the channels, a level CV on each, mutes that fade rather than cut, and a soft-clipping output stage

params.text: Silences that channel on each press and restores it on the next, fading over the time set on the menu rather than cutting
Silences that channel on each press and restores it on the next, fading over the time set on the menu rather than cutting
Sets that channel's level, from silence up to ten times the input
Sets that channel's level, from silence up to ten times the input
Sets the level of both outputs together, from silence to full
Sets the balance between the two channels: fully one way passes only channel I, fully the other only channel II, and centred passes both at half

inputs.text: The left signal of that channel
The right signal of that channel; with nothing patched it carries the left signal of the same channel
The left signal of that channel
The right signal of that channel; with nothing patched it carries the left signal of the same channel
Scales that channel's gain knob, 0-10V for none to all of it; a polyphonic cable scales each voice separately, and a one-channel cable scales every voice the same
Scales that channel's gain knob, 0-10V for none to all of it; a polyphonic cable scales each voice separately, and a one-channel cable scales every voice the same
Overrides the crossfader knob and moves it, ±5V covering the whole travel

outputs.text: The left side of the mix, soft-clipped through an anti-aliased tanh curve and clamped to -10 to 10V
The right side of the mix, soft-clipped through an anti-aliased tanh curve and clamped to -10 to 10V

notes: a polyphonic cable into a channel is mixed down to one signal by averaging its voices, unless the menu is set to sum them instead
menu: Output poly instead of mix — carries every voice out separately rather than mixing the polyphonic voices down to one stereo pair
Sum poly channels (instead of average) — adds the voices of a polyphonic input together rather than dividing the sum by the number of voices
Mute Fade Time (ms) — a slider setting how long a mute takes to fade in or out, 1 to 4000ms
